items.question: What attainment makes one dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are paired attainments
Great accomplishment is the stated result
Being dear to the yoginīs follows from this attainment
items.inference: One who attains enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: One may attain enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment, and become dear to the yoginīs.

items.question: Which chapter concludes with the emergence in Candra-dvīpa?
premises: The context is emergence in Candra-dvīpa
The section is identified by an ordinal number
The unit named is a chapter
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes in the context of emergence in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, having emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire
The posture involves standing
The stance is on one foot
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What determination of knowledge is requested to be revealed today?
premises: A determination of knowledge is sought
The request is addressed to the god
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest now
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make manifest today the determination of knowledge.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of eight groups of eight is sought to be known fully?
premises: The object is a division of eight groups of eight
The aim is to know it fully
The knowing is described as endless or complete
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and completely the division of the eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean 'in infinite detail' or 'without end'
items.plain_english: And to know fully, in all its extent, the division of the eight groups of eight.

items.question: How does the wheel become quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: A secret place is the context
The wheel is the subject of accomplishment
The accomplishment occurs quickly
items.inference: In the secret place, O Bhairava, the wheel is accomplished quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

items.question: Why is the question asked by the great goddess considered difficult for the gods to obtain?
premises: The speaker expresses strong approval
The great goddess has asked a question
The matter asked about is hard for the gods to obtain
items.inference: The speaker praises the great goddess for asking about a matter that is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
These are specific placements of seed syllables
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is placed in the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These placements are given as part of a sequence
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region and the syllable śa is in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

rows.grounds: states that wheels have been taught

items.question: What instruction follows after the place-wheels have been declared?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation remains to be taught
The listener is invited to hear it
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad to be visualized?
premises: The lotus is divine and eight-spoked
It is associated with the first octad
It is adorned by that first octad
items.inference: One should visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with an equal mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal mind
Village customs are identified as something to abandon
The abandonment is prescribed as a rule
items.inference: Through practice, one who has attained an equal mind should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer broadly to conventional social duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the customs of village life.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice according to the teaching given to the beloved?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned
These are presented as related attainments
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham could mean arresting or immobilizing bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized briefly for the goddess?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment
Transformation is named as an attainment
The teaching is given in brief
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may refer to bodily or situational transformation
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, there is immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: The lotus is the second one
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation
The practitioner makes forms
These forms can be made in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angry?
premises: Anger is the stated condition
The power is to destroy all
The scope includes the triple world with moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world, both moving and unmoving.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: The wheel is the third and great
It is associated with nine principles
Its function is described as liberating
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named
Seeing from very far away is named
These are presented as parallel attainments
items.inference: The practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and likewise the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should one practice meditation in solitude to assume many forms?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude
One should make many forms
One should be intent on meditation
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What attainment comes to one intent on constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice
Immortality is the stated result
The result is asserted emphatically
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What outcome regarding age and death follows from abstaining from food by day?
premises: Non-eating by day is the practice
Age and death are the matters affected
A future outcome is stated
items.inference: Through abstaining from food by day, one will go beyond death due to age.
uncertainties: gamiṣyate with vayo-mṛtyuṃ may mean 'will overcome death from aging'
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death brought by age.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant practice of this yoga?
premises: The means is constant practice through yoga
A specific age-form is indicated as two times eight years
This form becomes the practitioner's appearance
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from always contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: The contemplation is of a smoke-colored form
The contemplation is done always
The triple world is the object affected
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
